name: Sika MonoTop-910 N
paste:
SIKA MONOTOP®-910 N: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika MonoTop®-910 N, May 2025, Version 01.05 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/n/sika_monotop_-910n.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika MonoTop®-910 N where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.05).
1.2 Product description. Sika® MonoTop®-910 N is a cementitious, polymer modified one-component coating material containing silica fume used as bonding primer and reinforcement corrosion protection for reinforcement.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Suitable for control of anodic areas (Principle 11, method 11.1 of EN 1504-9)
    - Suitable as a bonding primer on concrete and mortar
    - Suitable in concrete repair as reinforcement corrosion protection
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.8.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika MonoTop®-910 N
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: BONDING PRIMER AND REINFORCEMENT CORROSION PROTECTION
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (May 2025, Version 01.05) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 1504-9: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Uses (p.1).
    - EN 1015-17: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Soluble chloride ion content (p.1).
    - AS1478.2:2005: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2).
    - EN 1542: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
    - EN 1504: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: System Information > System structure (p.2).
    - EN 1504-10: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Important Considerations (p.2).
    - ISO 8501-1: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel Reinforcement (p.3).
    - EN1504-10: referred to in instructions or limitations. Where: Application Instructions > Steel Reinforcement (p.3).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Easy to mix, just add water
    - User-friendly application
    - Excellent adhesion to concrete and steel
    - Good resistance to water and chloride penetration
    - Good mechanical strengths
    - Can be brushed on or applied using spray gun
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Portland cement, silica fume, re-dispersible polymer powder, selected aggregates and additives
    - Appearance and colour: Grey powder
    - Density: Fresh mortar density ~1.9 kg/l
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Soluble chloride ion content: ≤ 0.01 % (EN 1015-17)
    - Compressive strength: ~50 MPa after 28 days (AS1478.2:2005)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: ≥ 2.0 MPa after 28 days (EN 1542)
2.7 System structure. Sika MonoTop®-910 N is part of the range of Sika mortars complying with the relevant part of European Standard EN 1504 and comprising of: Bonding Primer / Reinforcement; Corrosion Protection
    | Sika MonoTop®-910 N | Normal Use |
    | Repair Mortars |
    | Sika Monotop-352 NFG | Class R3 Structural light weight re- |
    | pair mortar |
    | Sika Monotop-412 NFG | Class R4 Structural repair mortar |
    | Sika Monotop-612 N | Class R4 Structural high build repair |
    | mortar |
    | Sika Monotop-436 N | Class R4 Structural micro-concrete |
    | repair mortar |
    | Levelling Mortar |
    | Sika Monotop-723 N | Pore sealer and levelling mortar |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.8 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 10 kg pail and 20 kg bag
    - Shelf life: 12 months
    - Storage conditions: Store properly in undamaged original sealed packaging, in dry cool conditions between +5 °C and +35.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.05) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment.
    - Concrete
    - The concrete shall be thoroughly clean, free from dust, loose material, surface contamination and materials which reduce bond or prevent suction or wetting by repair materials. De-laminated, weak, damaged and deteriorated concrete and where necessary sound concrete shall be removed by suitable means.
3.3 Substrate quality / pre-treatment - Steel Reinforcement.
    - Rust, scale, mortar, concrete, dust and other loose and deleterious material which reduces bond or contributes to corrosion shall be removed. Surfaces shall be prepared using abrasive blast cleaning techniques or high pressure water-blasting to SA 2 (ISO 8501-1)
    - Reference shall be made to EN1504-10 for specific requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (May 2025, Version 01.05) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: For large volume: 2.0 - 2.2 litres of water per 10 kg pail; 4.0 - 4.4 litres of water per 20 kg bag; For small volume: 4 part of powder to 1 part of water by volume
    - Layer thickness: As bonding primer - sufficient to coat the concrete surface in a thin layer filling unevenness, pores and pits; As reinforcement corrosion protection - 2 mm minimum thickness
    - Pot Life: ~90 to 120 minutes at +20°C
    - Waiting time to overcoating: Apply concrete repair wet on wet with bonding primer; Apply concrete repair wet on dry reinforcement corrosion protection
    - Initial set time: ~ 5.5 hours
    - Final set time: ~ 7.5 hours
4.3 Consumption. Bonding Primer: This depends on the substrate roughness and thickness of layer applied. As a guide, ~1.5 – 2.0 kg of powder per m² per mm thick. Reinforcement Corrosion Protection: As a guide, ~2.0 kg of powder per m2 for 1mm layer thickness (in total min 2 layers)
4.4 Mixing. Sika MonoTop®-910 N can be mixed with a low speed (<500 rpm) electric drill mixer. In small quantity, Sika MonoTop®-910 N can also be mixed by volume in a mixing ratio of 4 part of powder by 1 part of water. Pour the water in the correct proportion into a suitable mixing container. While stirring slowly, add the powder to the water. Mixed thoroughly to the required consistency (brushable non-dripping consistency).
4.5 Application.
    - As a bonding primer
    - Apply by brush, roller or suitable spraying equipment to the prepared (pre-wetted) substrate. To achieve good bond, Sika® MonoTop®-910 N must be applied well into the substrate, filling all unevenness. Subsequent repair mortar must be applied while the bonding primer is still wet.
    - As reinforcement protection
    - Apply first layer approx. 1.0 mm thick, using medium hard brush or spray gun to cleaned reinforcement. When first coat is hard to the finger nail, for guidance~4 to 5 hours at 20°C, apply second layer approximately 1.0 mm thick.
4.6 Curing treatment. As reinforcement corrosion protection - protect the fresh mortar immediately from premature drying and contamination using an appropriate curing method.
4.7 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with water immediately after use. Hardened material can only be mechanically removed.
4.8 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Refer to the Method Statement for Concrete Repair using Sika MonoTop® system for more information or EN 1504-10
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong wind and/or rain
    - Do not add water over recommended dosage
    - Apply only to sound, prepared substrates

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5°C minimum; +30°C maximum
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5°C minimum; +30°C maximum
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.8):
    - Avoid application in direct sun and/or strong wind and/or rain
5.5 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Soluble chloride ion content: ≤ 0.01 % (EN 1015-17)
    - Compressive strength: ~50 MPa after 28 days (AS1478.2:2005)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: ≥ 2.0 MPa after 28 days (EN 1542)
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika MonoTop®-910 N, May 2025, Version 01.05, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/n/sika_monotop_-910n.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sika MonoTop®-910 N, version 27/10/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/7/sds-sika-monotop-910n.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
